subproblems.title: Translates of an orthonormally spanned subspace are embedded C^r submanifolds
subproblems.statement: Let P, d, r ∈ ℕ. Let Q ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be a linear subspace, let τ = (τ_0, …, τ_{d−1}) : Fin d → ℝ^P be an orthonormal family with span{τ_0, …, τ_{d−1}} = Q, and let a ∈ ℝ^P. Then the translate A := {y ∈ ℝ^P : y + a ∈ Q} = Q − a is a d-dimensional embedded C^r submanifold in the sense of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d A. That is, for every y ∈ A there exist an open V ⊆ ℝ^d, an open W ⊆ ℝ^P with y ∈ W, and a map ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P such that: ψ is C^r on V; ψ is injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ A; V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W; and the derivative fderiv ℝ ψ z is injective for every z ∈ V.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P d r : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (τ : Fin d → Euclid P) (a : Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) = Q → IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d {y | y + a ∈ Q}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is steps 2–4 of the supplied proof of the parent node codim1_zsl_offset_plane_inClassO (Lemma A-plane). The dimension n + 1 is replaced by a general d and the smoothness order 2 by a general r. The orthonormal frame τ, which the parent extracts from IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q, is taken here as a hypothesis.

Notation. ℝ^m = Euclid m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m), with Euclidean norm |v| = (Σ_j v_j²)^{1/2} and inner product ⟨v, w⟩ = Σ_j v_j w_j. Put A := {y ∈ ℝ^P : y + a ∈ Q}. Every step below also holds for d = 0, since empty sums are 0 and ℝ^0 = {0}.

1. (The linear map ι.) Define ι : ℝ^d → ℝ^P by ι(v) := Σ_{j<d} v_j·τ_j. It is the finite sum over j of the continuous linear maps v ↦ v_j·τ_j. Each of these is the coordinate functional EuclideanSpace.proj j followed by t ↦ t·τ_j, i.e. (EuclideanSpace.proj j).smulRight (τ j). Hence ι is a continuous linear map ℝ^d →L[ℝ] ℝ^P.

2. (ι is an isometry.) Let v ∈ ℝ^d. Orthonormality of τ means ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = 1 if i = j and 0 if i ≠ j. Therefore |ι(v)|² = ⟨Σ_i v_iτ_i, Σ_j v_jτ_j⟩ = Σ_i Σ_j v_i v_j ⟨τ_i, τ_j⟩ = Σ_j v_j·v_j = ⟨v, v⟩ = |v|². (Lemmas: Orthonormal.inner_sum, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, EuclideanSpace.inner_eq_star_dotProduct.) Both norms are nonnegative, so |ι(v)| = |v|.

3. (ι is injective.) Suppose ι(v) = ι(w). By linearity and step 2, |v − w| = |ι(v − w)| = |ι(v) − ι(w)| = 0, so v = w.

4. (The range of ι is Q.)
(a) Let v ∈ ℝ^d. Each τ_j lies in span{τ_0, …, τ_{d−1}} = Q, and Q is closed under scalar multiplication and finite sums. Hence ι(v) = Σ_j v_jτ_j ∈ Q.
(b) Conversely, let q ∈ Q = span{τ_j : j < d}. The index type Fin d is finite, so there is c : Fin d → ℝ with q = Σ_j c_j·τ_j (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). Let v ∈ ℝ^d be the vector with coordinates v_j = c_j (WithLp.toLp 2 c). Then ι(v) = q.

5. (A global parametrization.) Define ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P by ψ(v) := ι(v) − a. For z ∈ ℝ^P:
z ∈ A ⟺ z + a ∈ Q ⟺ z + a = ι(v) for some v ∈ ℝ^d (step 4) ⟺ z = ψ(v) for some v ∈ ℝ^d.
Hence ψ(ℝ^d) = A.

6. (The chart clauses at a point.) Let y ∈ A. Take V := ℝ^d (the whole of Euclid d), W := ℝ^P (the whole of Euclid P), and ψ from step 5.
(a) V and W are open because they are whole spaces, and y ∈ W.
(b) ψ is a continuous linear map minus a constant, so ψ is C^∞ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, ContDiff.sub, contDiff_const). In particular ContDiffOn ℝ r ψ V.
(c) Let v, w ∈ V with ψ(v) = ψ(w). Then ι(v) − a = ι(w) − a, so ι(v) = ι(w), and v = w by step 3. Thus InjOn ψ V.
(d) ψ(V) = ψ(ℝ^d) = A = ℝ^P ∩ A = W ∩ A, by step 5.
(e) Let K ⊆ W be compact. Since V = ℝ^d, V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) = ψ^{−1}(K).
- This set is closed: K is closed (a compact subset of the Hausdorff space ℝ^P) and ψ is continuous.
- This set is bounded: K is bounded, so there is R ∈ ℝ with |z| ≤ R for all z ∈ K (isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le). If ψ(v) ∈ K, then by step 2, |v| = |ι(v)| = |ψ(v) + a| ≤ |ψ(v)| + |a| ≤ R + |a|.
- A closed and bounded subset of ℝ^d is compact (Heine–Borel; ℝ^d is a proper metric space; isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded).
Hence V ∩ ψ^{−1}(K) is compact.
(f) Let z ∈ V. A continuous linear map is its own derivative at every point (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt), and subtracting the constant a does not change the derivative (HasFDerivAt.sub_const). So fderiv ℝ ψ z = ι, which is injective by step 3.

7. (Conclusion.) For every y ∈ A, step 6 provides V, W and ψ satisfying every clause in the definition of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d A. Hence IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d {y | y + a ∈ Q}. ∎
proof_key_steps: ι(v) := Σ_j v_jτ_j is a continuous linear map ℝ^d → ℝ^P with |ι(v)| = |v| by orthonormality, so ι is injective.
The range of ι is span τ = Q, so ψ(v) := ι(v) − a satisfies ψ(ℝ^d) = A = {y | y + a ∈ Q}.
At each y ∈ A take V = ℝ^d and W = ℝ^P: ψ is C^∞, injective on V, and ψ(V) = W ∩ A.
Each preimage ψ^{−1}(K) of a compact K is closed and bounded (|v| ≤ R + |a|), hence compact by Heine–Borel. fderiv ψ ≡ ι is injective, so all clauses of IsEmbeddedSubmanifold r d A hold.

subproblems.title: The tangent space of a translated linear subspace is the subspace
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P (= Euclid P) be a linear subspace, and let a, y ∈ ℝ^P with y + a ∈ Q. Put A := {z ∈ ℝ^P : z + a ∈ Q} = Q − a. Then tangentSpace A y = Q as subsets of ℝ^P. Here tangentSpace A y is the set of v ∈ ℝ^P for which there is γ : ℝ → ℝ^P that is C¹ on (−1, 1), maps (−1, 1) into A, satisfies γ(0) = y, and has derivative v at 0 (HasDerivAt γ v 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a y : Euclid P), y + a ∈ Q → tangentSpace {z | z + a ∈ Q} y = (Q : Set (Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is step 6 of the supplied proof of the parent node codim1_zsl_offset_plane_inClassO (Lemma A-plane), together with the closedness of Q from its step 5. It is stated for an arbitrary point y of A := {z ∈ ℝ^P : z + a ∈ Q} = Q − a.

Recall the definition: tangentSpace A y is the set of v ∈ ℝ^P for which there exists γ : ℝ → ℝ^P such that γ is C¹ on (−1, 1), γ((−1, 1)) ⊆ A, γ(0) = y, and HasDerivAt γ v 0.

1. (Q is closed.) Q is a linear subspace of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P. Hence Q is finite-dimensional, and therefore a closed subset of ℝ^P (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional).

2. (tangentSpace A y ⊆ Q.) Let v ∈ tangentSpace A y and choose γ as in the definition. The C¹ hypothesis is not needed for this inclusion.
(a) Define the difference quotients s(t) := (t − 0)^{−1}·(γ(t) − γ(0)). Since HasDerivAt γ v 0, s(t) → v as t → 0 with t ≠ 0, i.e. along the punctured-neighbourhood filter 𝓝[≠] 0. (Lemma hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope; slope_def_module identifies slope γ 0 t with (t − 0)^{−1}·(γ(t) − γ(0)).)
(b) The open interval (−1, 1) contains 0, so it is a neighbourhood of 0 and belongs to 𝓝[≠] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhds, nhdsWithin_le_nhds). For t ∈ (−1, 1), γ(t) ∈ A, i.e. γ(t) + a ∈ Q. Also γ(0) + a = y + a ∈ Q by hypothesis.
(c) For such t, γ(t) − γ(0) = (γ(t) + a) − (γ(0) + a) ∈ Q, because Q is closed under subtraction. Then s(t) = (t − 0)^{−1}·(γ(t) − γ(0)) ∈ Q, because Q is closed under scalar multiplication. So s(t) ∈ Q for all t in a member of 𝓝[≠] 0.
(d) The filter 𝓝[≠] 0 on ℝ is nontrivial, s tends to v along it, and s eventually takes values in the closed set Q (step 1). So the limit v lies in Q (IsClosed.mem_of_tendsto).

3. (Q ⊆ tangentSpace A y.) Let v ∈ Q and define γ : ℝ → ℝ^P by γ(t) := y + t·v.
(a) γ is a constant plus the product of the C^∞ function t ↦ t with the constant vector v, so γ is C^∞. In particular γ is C¹ on (−1, 1).
(b) For every t ∈ ℝ, γ(t) + a = (y + a) + t·v ∈ Q, since y + a ∈ Q, v ∈ Q, and Q is a linear subspace. Hence γ(t) ∈ A for every t; in particular γ maps (−1, 1) into A.
(c) γ(0) = y + 0·v = y.
(d) t ↦ t has derivative 1 at 0 (hasDerivAt_id), so t ↦ t·v has derivative 1·v = v at 0 (HasDerivAt.smul_const). Adding the constant y does not change the derivative (HasDerivAt.const_add). Hence HasDerivAt γ v 0.
By (a)–(d), γ witnesses v ∈ tangentSpace A y.

4. (Conclusion.) Steps 2 and 3 give both inclusions, so tangentSpace {z | z + a ∈ Q} y = Q as subsets of ℝ^P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Q is a finite-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P, hence closed.
⊆: for t ∈ (−1, 1) ∖ {0}, the slope t^{−1}(γ(t) − γ(0)) = t^{−1}((γ(t) + a) − (y + a)) lies in Q and tends to v along 𝓝[≠] 0. Closedness of Q gives v ∈ Q.
⊇: for v ∈ Q, the line γ(t) = y + t·v is C^∞, stays in A because (y + a) + t·v ∈ Q, and has γ(0) = y and HasDerivAt γ v 0.
